title: Getting Started with FastAPI
description: Create a FastAPI project from an empty folder, run it locally with Uvicorn, open the automatic documentation it generates, save the packages it needs, and keep configuration such as secrets in an .env file instead of in the code.
outline: Create the project folder
Create and activate a virtual environment on Windows and on macOS/Linux
Install FastAPI and Uvicorn with pip
Create your first application and understand each line of the code
Run the application with `uvicorn` and reload on change
Open the automatic API documentation at `/docs`
Save project dependencies with `pip freeze` into `requirements.txt`
Store configuration in an `.env` file
Protect local files with `.gitignore`
Run the app directly with Python under the `__main__` guard (alternative)

title: Routes and Parameters
description: Create endpoints for the common HTTP methods, read values from the URL as path and query parameters, give them defaults, validate them, read headers and cookies, restrict a value to a fixed set of choices, and see why the order of routes changes which one answers.
outline: Create a route with `@app.get`
Common HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE
Path parameters
Multiple path parameters
Query parameters
Optional query parameters and defaults
Combine path and query parameters
Validate parameters with `Path()` and `Query()`
Read request headers and cookies with `Header()` and `Cookie()`
Restrict values with `Enum`
Route order matters: a fixed path before a path parameter

title: Request Body and Pydantic
description: Learn how an API receives JSON data in a request body, describe that data with a Pydantic model, let FastAPI check it before your function runs, and build models with optional fields, validation rules, lists and nested models.
outline: What a request body is and when to send one
Create a Pydantic model with `BaseModel`
Receive the request body in a FastAPI endpoint
Required and optional fields, and default values
Add simple validation rules with `Field()`
Use a list inside a model with `list[...]`
Use a nested model
Why custom validator decorators wait until the basics are comfortable

title: Response Handling, Forms and Errors
description: Choose the right status code for each answer, control which fields go back to the client, raise HTTP errors with a clear message, return a custom JSON response, set response headers and cookies, and receive simple HTML form fields.
outline: Set a status code with `status_code`, and why status `204` sends no body
Filter returned data with `response_model`
Include or exclude response fields with `response_model_exclude`
Raise an HTTP error with `HTTPException`
Return a custom JSON response with `JSONResponse`
Set response headers and cookies with `set_cookie`
Receive form fields with `Form()`

title: Dependency Injection
description: Write small reusable functions that FastAPI runs before an endpoint, pass their results in with Depends, chain one dependency on another, set up and clean up resources with yield, use a class as a dependency, and apply dependencies to a whole router or application.
outline: Why use dependencies: the repeated code they remove
Create your first dependency with `Depends`
Reuse a dependency in several endpoints
A dependency with a parameter
A dependency that uses another dependency (sub-dependencies)
Use `yield` for setup and cleanup
Class-based dependency
Apply dependencies to a router or application with `dependencies=`

title: Database Integration with SQLAlchemy
description: Connect FastAPI to a SQLite database with SQLAlchemy, define a table as a Python class, give each request its own database session, and build create, read, update and delete endpoints for students, then see what a real project adds with migrations.
outline: Install SQLAlchemy
Create the beginner project folder
Create the database connection with `create_engine` and a table model with `DeclarativeBase`
Understand the setup: `sessionmaker`, one `Session` per request through `get_db`
Add the create endpoint
Add endpoints to read one student and all students
Add the update endpoint and how `PUT` replaces a whole record
Add the delete endpoint
Run and test the CRUD endpoints in the docs page
Next steps for real projects: database migrations with `Alembic`

title: Modular Application Development
description: Split a growing FastAPI application into a package of files, put each group of routes in its own APIRouter, connect the routers in main.py with a prefix and tags, run the project from the right folder, and trace how the files connect.
outline: Why split an application into files
Create the folders: a `routers` package with `__init__.py`
Create the students router with `APIRouter`
Create the teachers router
Connect routers in main.py with `include_router`
Understand `prefix` and `tags`
Run the modular project and see how the files connect

title: Authentication and Authorization
description: Tell authentication apart from authorization, store passwords as hashes and never as plain text, understand bearer tokens and JWTs, build a learning login flow that issues a token and protects routes, test it, and list what a production identity system still needs.
outline: Authentication vs authorization, and status codes `401` and `403`
Never store plain-text passwords: hash them with `pwdlib`
Understand a bearer token and a JWT made with `PyJWT`
Login with `OAuth2PasswordRequestForm` and issue a token
Protect routes with `OAuth2PasswordBearer` and `get_current_user`
Keep the secret key in an environment variable
Test the login and protected-route flow
What the example leaves out: token expiry, refresh and revocation, OAuth2 `scopes`, and `API key` authentication

title: Middleware and Security
description: See how middleware wraps every request and response, write a custom middleware that measures request time, configure CORS so a frontend can call the API, use FastAPI's built-in middleware, add a security header, and learn why middleware order, rate limiting and safe logging matter.
outline: How middleware works around each request and response
Create simple custom middleware with `@app.middleware` and `call_next`
Configure CORS for a frontend with `CORSMiddleware`
Built-in middleware: `GZipMiddleware`, `TrustedHostMiddleware` and `HTTPSRedirectMiddleware`
Add a basic security header such as `X-Content-Type-Options`
Middleware order and which one runs first
Rate limiting and safe logging that never records secrets

title: File Handling
description: Receive one or many uploaded files, read their name, type and contents, reject files that are too big or the wrong type, save them in chunks under a generated name, let clients download files from a safe folder, and stream large or generated content.
outline: Install file upload support with `python-multipart`
Receive a file with `UploadFile` and `File()`
Read a file's name, content type and contents
Check size and type, answer `413` for a file that is too big
Save a file in chunks with a generated name from `uuid`
Upload multiple files
Download a file with `FileResponse` from a safe path
Stream generated or large content with `StreamingResponse`

title: Asynchronous Programming and Background Tasks
description: Compare synchronous and asynchronous functions, decide when an endpoint should use def or async def, run several async tasks together with asyncio.gather, schedule small jobs to run after the response with BackgroundTasks, and know when a real task queue is needed instead.
outline: Synchronous and asynchronous functions with `async def` and `await`
Use def or `async def` in a FastAPI endpoint?
Run multiple async tasks together with `asyncio.gather`
Add a background task with `BackgroundTasks`
Add more than one background task with `add_task`
When not to use `BackgroundTasks`, and what a queue such as `Celery` does instead

title: Advanced API Development
description: Add the features a real API needs: pagination, filtering and sorting of lists, a custom exception handler, lifespan startup and shutdown, two-way WebSockets, one-way server-sent events, static files, and versioned routes that let old clients keep working.
outline: Pagination with `skip` and `limit`
Add filtering and sorting with a `sort` parameter
Create a custom exception handler with `exception_handler`
Lifespan events with `lifespan` and `asynccontextmanager`
WebSockets with `WebSocket`
Server-Sent Events (SSE): the concept and how it differs from WebSockets
A small Server-Sent Events example with `text/event-stream`
Serve static files with `StaticFiles`
API versioning with a `/v1` prefix

title: Testing and Debugging
description: Write automated tests for a FastAPI app with pytest and TestClient, check successful and failing responses including validation errors, replace dependencies during tests, keep test data in its own database, test async endpoints, and use logging to find a problem.
outline: Install testing packages: `pytest` and `httpx`
Create a small application to test
Write the first test with `TestClient`
Test a POST request
Test error responses and validation errors with status `422`
Run tests with pytest and read the result
Dependency overrides with `dependency_overrides`
Test database-backed endpoints with an isolated test database
Test async endpoints with `AsyncClient`
Debug with `logging`

title: Real-World Deployment with Render
description: Take a finished FastAPI project to production on Render: prepare the project, keep secrets out of source control, pin dependencies, set the start command, connect a hosted database and migrate it, add a health endpoint, then use a custom domain, logs, rollback and an optional Docker setup.
outline: Understand the deployment flow from code to a live URL
Prepare the project folder for deployment
Keep secrets out of source control
Prepare dependencies in requirements.txt
Configure the start command with `--host 0.0.0.0` and `$PORT`
Connect the production database through `DATABASE_URL`
Database migrations with `alembic upgrade head`
Deploy on Render step by step
Add a health endpoint at `/health`
Custom domain and HTTPS
Logs, monitoring and `rollback`
Uploaded files and background jobs need persistent storage in production
Docker as an optional deployment extension with a `Dockerfile`
Final deployment checklist

title: Capstone: Institute Enquiry API
description: Build one complete FastAPI service for the institute's admissions team that uses every chapter: Pydantic models for enquiries, SQLAlchemy storage loaded from the institute's enquiry records, routers split by area, counsellor login with tokens, paginated and filtered lists, CSV file import and export, a background follow-up task, pytest tests that prove each milestone, and a deployment-ready start command with a health endpoint.
outline: The problem: what the enquiry API does for the admissions team, and an architecture figure
Milestone 1: project setup, settings from `.env` and a `/health` endpoint (Chapters 1 and 14)
Milestone 2: enquiry models with `BaseModel` and `Field()`, and response models (Chapters 3 and 4)
Milestone 3: SQLAlchemy storage, a `get_db` dependency and CRUD endpoints (Chapters 5 and 6)
Milestone 4: split the app into routers with `APIRouter` (Chapter 7)
Milestone 5: counsellor login with a JWT and protected routes using `Depends` (Chapter 8)
Milestone 6: request-timing middleware and CORS with `CORSMiddleware` (Chapter 9)
Milestone 7: paginated, filtered and sorted enquiry lists with `skip` and `limit` (Chapters 2 and 12)
Milestone 8: CSV import with `UploadFile` and CSV export with `StreamingResponse` (Chapter 10)
Milestone 9: a follow-up reminder with `BackgroundTasks` (Chapter 11)
Milestone 10: tests for every milestone with `TestClient` and `dependency_overrides` (Chapter 13)
Run the whole thing locally and with the production start command
Extension ideas
